languages.name: NASM
languages.description: Netwide Assembler reference focused on x86-64 systems programming, helper routines, ABI boundaries, and WynCommand integration.

categories.name: Registers and Data Movement
categories.description: Core x86-64 registers and movement instructions.

entries.title: General-purpose registers
entries.summary: Use x86-64 general-purpose registers such as RAX, RBX, RCX, RDX, RSI, RDI, RSP, RBP, and R8-R15.
entries.definition: Use x86-64 general-purpose registers such as RAX, RBX, RCX, RDX, RSI, RDI, RSP, RBP, and R8-R15.
entries.mental_model: Registers are the CPU's tiny, ultra-fast scratchpad.
entries.gotchas: Some registers have ABI-defined roles across calls.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Loads 42 into RAX, then copies it into RBX.

entries.title: MOV
entries.summary: Copy data between registers, memory, and immediates.
entries.definition: Copy data between registers, memory, and immediates.
entries.mental_model: MOV copies bits; it does not conceptually move ownership.
entries.gotchas: Memory-to-memory MOV is generally not allowed.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Copies an immediate into RAX, then stores RAX to memory.

entries.title: LEA
entries.summary: Compute an effective address without dereferencing it.
entries.definition: Compute an effective address without dereferencing it.
entries.mental_model: Treat LEA as integer/address arithmetic using addressing syntax.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Computes an address expression and stores the address in RAX.

entries.title: MOVZX
entries.summary: Copy a smaller unsigned value into a larger register and zero-extend it.
entries.definition: Copy a smaller unsigned value into a larger register and zero-extend it.
entries.mental_model: Promote a small unsigned integer without preserving garbage in upper bits.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Loads one byte and clears the upper bits of EAX.

categories.name: Arithmetic and Logic
categories.description: Integer arithmetic, comparisons, and bit operations.

entries.title: ADD and SUB
entries.summary: Perform integer addition and subtraction.
entries.signature: add dst, src / sub dst, src
entries.definition: Perform integer addition and subtraction.
entries.mental_model: Mutate the destination register in place.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
mov rax, 10
add rax, 5
sub rax, 3
examples.explanation: Leaves 12 in RAX.

entries.title: IMUL
entries.summary: Perform signed integer multiplication.
entries.definition: Perform signed integer multiplication.
entries.mental_model: Signed multiplication with convenient two-operand forms.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Leaves 42 in RAX.

entries.title: CMP
entries.summary: Compare two operands by setting CPU flags as if subtraction occurred.
entries.definition: Compare two operands by setting CPU flags as if subtraction occurred.
entries.mental_model: CMP prepares flags for a later conditional instruction.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Branches if RAX equals zero.

entries.title: TEST
entries.summary: Perform a bitwise AND for flags without storing the result.
entries.definition: Perform a bitwise AND for flags without storing the result.
entries.mental_model: Use TEST when you care about flags, not the AND result.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Efficiently checks whether RAX is zero.

entries.title: Bitwise operations
entries.summary: Manipulate bits with AND, OR, XOR, NOT, SHL, and SHR.
entries.definition: Manipulate bits with AND, OR, XOR, NOT, SHL, and SHR.
entries.mental_model: Think masks, flags, packing, and powers of two.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
xor eax, eax
mov ecx, 1
shl ecx, 4
examples.explanation: Clears EAX and shifts ECX left by four bits.

categories.name: Control Flow and Calls
categories.description: Branches, loops, functions, and stack discipline.

entries.title: JMP
entries.summary: Perform an unconditional branch.
entries.definition: Perform an unconditional branch.
entries.mental_model: Replace fall-through execution with an explicit destination.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Skips over the MOV instruction.

entries.title: Conditional jumps
entries.summary: Branch based on CPU flags using JE, JNE, JL, JG, JB, JA, and related instructions.
entries.definition: Branch based on CPU flags using JE, JNE, JL, JG, JB, JA, and related instructions.
entries.mental_model: CMP/TEST sets flags; Jcc consumes them.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Chooses a path based on the comparison.

entries.title: CALL and RET
entries.summary: Call a function and return using the stack-stored return address.
entries.definition: Call a function and return using the stack-stored return address.
entries.mental_model: CALL is controlled stack bookkeeping plus a jump.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
call add_two
; ...
add_two:
    add rax, 2
    ret
examples.explanation: CALL pushes the return address; RET pops it.

entries.title: PUSH and POP
entries.summary: Save and restore stack values.
entries.definition: Save and restore stack values.
entries.mental_model: RSP moves as values are pushed and popped.
entries.gotchas: Maintain ABI-required stack alignment before external calls.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
push rbx
mov rbx, 99
pop rbx
examples.explanation: Temporarily preserves RBX.

entries.title: System V AMD64 calling convention
entries.summary: Pass integer/pointer arguments in RDI, RSI, RDX, RCX, R8, and R9 on Linux/macOS System V x86-64.
entries.signature: rdi, rsi, rdx, rcx, r8, r9
entries.definition: Pass integer/pointer arguments in RDI, RSI, RDX, RCX, R8, and R9 on Linux/macOS System V x86-64.
entries.mental_model: Registers are agreed-upon mail slots between caller and callee.
entries.gotchas: Windows x64 uses a different convention.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
my_func:
    mov rax, rdi
    add rax, rsi
    ret
examples.explanation: Returns the sum of the first two integer arguments.

entries.title: Memory addressing
entries.summary: Address memory with base, index, scale, and displacement expressions.

entries.mental_model: Effective addresses are arithmetic expressions evaluated by the CPU.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Loads a 32-bit element indexed by RCX.

entries.title: Sections
entries.summary: Organize code and data into sections such as .text, .data, .rodata, and .bss.
entries.definition: Organize code and data into sections such as .text, .data, .rodata, and .bss.
entries.mental_model: Sections tell the linker what kind of bytes you are defining.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Declares writable data and then switches to code.

entries.title: Labels
entries.summary: Name instruction or data addresses.
entries.definition: Name instruction or data addresses.
entries.mental_model: A label is a symbolic address resolved by the assembler/linker.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Uses a label as a branch target.

entries.title: DB, DW, DD, DQ
entries.summary: Define byte, word, doubleword, and quadword data.
entries.definition: Define byte, word, doubleword, and quadword data.
entries.mental_model: Directives emit raw bytes into the object file.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Defines a null-terminated byte string and a 64-bit integer.

entries.title: EQU
entries.summary: Define an assembly-time constant.
entries.definition: Define an assembly-time constant.
entries.mental_model: EQU is textual/assembly-time meaning, not runtime memory.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Creates symbolic constants without storage.

entries.title: GLOBAL and EXTERN
entries.summary: Export symbols and reference symbols provided by other object files.
entries.definition: Export symbols and reference symbols provided by other object files.
entries.mental_model: GLOBAL opens a door outward; EXTERN declares a door expected elsewhere.

examples.title: Example
examples.explanation: Exports one function and declares an external dependency.

categories.name: Linux Syscalls
categories.description: Direct kernel entry points useful for low-level helpers.

entries.title: syscall instruction
entries.summary: Enter the Linux kernel using the x86-64 syscall ABI.
entries.definition: Enter the Linux kernel using the x86-64 syscall ABI.
entries.mental_model: Place the syscall number and arguments in ABI-defined registers, then cross into the kernel.
entries.gotchas: Syscall numbers and conventions are OS/architecture specific.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
mov rax, 60
xor rdi, rdi
syscall
examples.explanation: Invokes exit(0) on Linux x86-64.

entries.title: write syscall
entries.summary: Write bytes to a file descriptor directly through Linux.
entries.definition: Write bytes to a file descriptor directly through Linux.
entries.mental_model: A minimal path from your process to the kernel without libc.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
mov rax, 1
mov rdi, 1
lea rsi, [rel msg]
mov rdx, msg_len
syscall
examples.explanation: Writes msg to stdout.
